topic_ko: 스놉 효과 — 제품이 희귀할수록 가치 있게 여기고, 흔해지면 흥미를 잃는 소비 심리

passage: Some shoppers lose their desire for an item the moment everyone else seems to have it.
This reaction is known as the snob effect.
People affected by it value goods mainly because few others can get them.
Picture a brand that sells just 500 pairs of special sneakers.
Fans rush to buy them since they are so hard to find.
But when the brand later makes millions of pairs, many of those fans walk away.
Owning the shoes no longer makes them feel different from others.
For this reason, companies often keep their products limited to make them look rare and special.
choices: why mass production always lowers the quality of sneakers
how a product’s rarity affects some consumers’ desire to buy it
the reasons people follow their friends’ shopping choices
ways to save money when buying limited-edition goods
the history of famous sneaker brands and their designs
theme.explanation_ko: 흔해지면 사고 싶은 마음이 사라지고, 희귀할 때 더 원한다는 내용이므로 ‘제품의 희소성이 일부 소비자의 구매 욕구에 미치는 영향’이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 대량 생산과 품질은 무관하다. ③ 친구를 따라 사는 것은 반대 개념(밴드왜건 효과)이다. ④ 돈을 아끼는 방법은 나오지 않는다. ⑤ 운동화 브랜드의 역사는 다루지 않는다.

passage: Most of us like things that are popular, but some people feel the opposite way.
They want a product most when it is rare or hard to get.
If only a few hundred pairs of sneakers are sold, these buyers are eager to own a pair.
Once the same sneakers are produced in huge numbers, however, the shoes lose their appeal.
This is the snob effect, and it works in the opposite direction from the bandwagon effect.
While bandwagon buyers want what everyone has, snob buyers want what makes them different.
Knowing this, companies release limited-edition and luxury goods to create a feeling of rarity.
Buyers who value being unique are often ready to pay more for such goods.
choices: 유행하는 제품을 사야 사회에서 인정받을 수 있다.
한정판 제품은 품질이 좋아서 비싸게 팔린다.
기업은 제품을 대량 생산해야 더 많은 이익을 얻는다.
어떤 소비자들은 제품이 희소할수록 더 가치 있게 여기고, 흔해지면 관심을 잃는다.
소비자는 친구들이 산 물건을 따라 사는 경향이 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 희귀할 때 원하고 흔해지면 매력을 잃는 스놉 효과를 설명하는 글이므로 ④가 요지이다.
gist.distractor_ko: ① 유행을 따르는 것은 스놉 효과와 반대이다. ② 품질 이야기는 없다. ③ 대량 생산하면 오히려 흥미를 잃는다. ⑤ 밴드왜건 효과의 설명이다.

passage: Some shoppers lose their desire for an item the moment everyone else seems to have it.
This reaction is known as the snob effect.
People affected by it value goods mainly because few others can get them.
Picture a brand that sells just 500 pairs of special sneakers.
Fans rush to buy them since they are so hard to find.
But when the brand later makes millions of pairs, many of those fans walk away.
Owning the shoes no longer makes them feel different from others.
For this reason, companies often keep their products limited to make them look rare and special.
choices: Rare Means Special: Why Some Buyers Avoid Popular Items
Follow the Crowd and Shop Smart
How Sneakers Are Made in Factories
The Hidden Costs of Cheap Products
Why Prices Always Rise over Time
title.explanation_ko: 드물어야 특별하게 느끼고, 인기 있는 물건은 피하는 소비자를 다루므로 ①이 제목으로 알맞다.
title.distractor_ko: ② 군중을 따르는 것은 반대 내용이다. ③ 운동화 제조 과정은 나오지 않는다. ④ 싼 제품의 숨은 비용은 무관하다. ⑤ 가격 상승 일반론은 다루지 않는다.

passage: A sneaker company decides to make only 500 pairs of a new design.
Because the shoes are so hard to get, many people line up to buy them.
Months later, the company produces millions of the same pair.
Suddenly, some of the first buyers stop wearing them.
Their shoes have become just another pair in the crowd.
This is a typical example of the snob effect.
People who are influenced by it value products that are rare or exclusive.
When too many others own the same item, it loses its charm for them.
implication.underlined: just another pair in the crowd
choices: a pair that is too small for most people to wear
a pair that was made with cheaper materials
a pair that no longer makes its owner stand out
a pair that is sold at a much higher price
a pair that the company refused to produce again
implication.explanation_ko: 수백만 켤레가 생산되어 누구나 가진 흔한 신발이 되었다는 뜻이므로, 더 이상 주인을 돋보이게 하지 못한다는 ③이 알맞다.
implication.distractor_ko: ① 크기 이야기는 없다. ② 재료가 싸졌다는 말은 없다. ④ 가격이 올랐다는 내용이 아니다. ⑤ 회사는 오히려 대량으로 다시 생산했다.

passage: Why do some people stop wanting a product once it becomes popular?
The answer lies in the snob effect, which refers to people’s tendency to value things that are rare.
Imagine a company that releases only 500 pairs of limited-edition sneakers.
Many people want them because they are difficult to obtain.
Later, however, the company produces millions of the same sneakers, and some buyers lose interest.
They no longer feel special, since so many other people own the same shoes.
That is why companies release limited products to create a sense of rarity.
Consumers who value uniqueness may even be willing paying higher prices for them.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
grammar.explanation_ko: be willing 뒤에는 to부정사가 와서 ‘기꺼이 ~하다’를 나타내므로 be willing paying 은 be willing to pay 가 되어야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① stop -ing ‘~하는 것을 그만두다’. ② 앞의 the snob effect 를 보충 설명하는 계속적 용법 which 와 단수 동사 refers. ③ 「difficult + to부정사」. ④ 감각동사 feel + 형용사 보어.

passage: Some consumers value a product because it is rare or exclusive.
As more people buy the same product, it becomes more attractive to these consumers.
Picture a company that releases only 500 pairs of limited-edition sneakers.
Many people want them because they are hard to obtain.
If the company later makes millions of the same sneakers, some buyers lose interest.
This snob effect is the opposite of the bandwagon effect, in which people follow the crowd.
Companies make use of it by releasing luxury goods to create a sense of scarcity.
Buyers who value uniqueness may then pay higher prices for these goods.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
vocab.explanation_ko: 스놉 효과의 소비자에게는 많은 사람이 같은 제품을 살수록 제품이 ‘덜’ 매력적이 되므로 more attractive 는 less attractive 가 되어야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 희귀해서 가치 있게 여긴다. ③ 흔해지면 흥미를 ‘잃는다’. ④ 군중을 따르는 밴드왜건 효과의 ‘반대’이다. ⑤ 명품으로 ‘희소성’의 느낌을 만든다.

passage: When a new product appears, some people rush to buy it simply because everyone else does.
Others react in the opposite way.
They are attracted to a product only while it is rare or hard to get.
When a company sells just 500 pairs of special sneakers, these buyers eagerly line up.
But once millions of the same sneakers fill the stores, they lose interest.
For these consumers, the value of a product depends on ______________________.
This tendency is called the snob effect.
It explains why companies often sell limited editions at high prices.
choices: how useful it is in everyday life
how many of their friends recommend it
how cheaply it can be produced
how few other people own it
how long it lasts after purchase
blank.explanation_ko: 희귀할 때만 끌리고 흔해지면 흥미를 잃으므로, 이들에게 제품의 가치는 ‘그것을 가진 사람이 얼마나 적은가’에 달려 있다.
blank.distractor_ko: ① 쓸모, ③ 생산 비용, ⑤ 내구성은 본문에서 다루지 않는다. ② 친구의 추천을 따르는 것은 반대 성향이다.

irrelevant.intro: The snob effect describes people’s tendency to value a product because it is rare or exclusive.
sentences: When a company releases only a small number of sneakers, many people want to own a pair.
However, when the same shoes are later produced in large numbers, some buyers lose interest.
Sneakers with thick soles help protect runners’ knees from injury.
These buyers no longer feel special because so many other people own the same shoes.
For this reason, companies release limited-edition goods to create a sense of rarity.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
irrelevant.explanation_ko: ③은 운동화 밑창의 기능(무릎 보호)에 관한 내용으로, 희소성과 소비 심리를 다루는 글의 흐름과 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①② 한정판 → 대량 생산의 예시, ④ 흥미를 잃는 이유, ⑤ 기업의 활용으로 모두 흐름에 맞다.

order.given: Why do some people lose interest in a product as soon as it becomes popular? This behavior is known as the snob effect, people’s tendency to value things that are rare or exclusive.

blocks.A: For example, suppose a company releases only 500 pairs of limited-edition sneakers. Many people want them because they are so hard to obtain.
blocks.B: Companies have learned from this pattern of excitement and disappointment. They release limited-edition or luxury products to create a sense of rarity, and buyers who value uniqueness are willing to pay more.
blocks.C: Later, however, the company produces millions of the same pair. Some of the first buyers then lose interest, because owning the shoes no longer makes them feel special.

order.explanation_ko: 스놉 효과 정의(주어진 글) → For example 로 한정판 500켤레 예시(A) → Later, however 로 대량 생산 후 흥미 상실(C) → 이 ‘열광과 실망의 패턴’을 이용하는 기업(B) 순이다.
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 the company·the same pair 는 (A)의 회사와 운동화를 받으므로 (A) 뒤에 와야 하고, (B)의 this pattern of excitement and disappointment 는 (A)의 열광과 (C)의 실망을 모두 받으므로 맨 끝이다.

insert.insert_sentence: As a result, these companies can charge higher prices, since buyers who value uniqueness are willing to pay more.

passage_marked.text: The snob effect is people’s tendency to value products that are rare or exclusive.
When only 500 pairs of special sneakers are released, many people want them because they are hard to get.
If millions of the same sneakers are produced later, however, some buyers lose interest.
Unlike bandwagon buyers, these people want products that help them stand out from the crowd.
That is why companies release limited-edition or luxury products to create a sense of rarity.

choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 these companies 는 마지막 문장의 companies 를 가리키고, ‘그 결과’ 더 높은 가격을 받을 수 있다는 결과이므로 ⑤에 들어간다.
insert.distractor_ko: ①~④ 앞에는 companies 가 한 번도 나오지 않아 these companies 가 가리킬 대상이 없다.

passage: Most of us like things that are popular, but some people feel the opposite way.
They want a product most when it is rare or hard to get.
If only a few hundred pairs of sneakers are sold, these buyers are eager to own a pair.
Once the same sneakers are produced in huge numbers, however, the shoes lose their appeal.
This is the snob effect, and it works in the opposite direction from the bandwagon effect.
While bandwagon buyers want what everyone has, snob buyers want what makes them different.
Knowing this, companies release limited-edition and luxury goods to create a feeling of rarity.
Buyers who value being unique are often ready to pay more for such goods.
summary.summary_template: Some consumers want a product more when it is __(A)__, but they lose interest once it becomes __(B)__.
summary.explanation_ko: 희귀할(rare) 때 더 원하고 흔해지면(common) 흥미를 잃는다는 스놉 효과의 요약이다.
summary.distractor_ko: ② 가격은 다루지 않는다. ③④ 두 낱말의 관계가 거꾸로이다. ⑤ 새것·헌것의 문제가 아니다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 「difficult + to부정사」 ‘~하기 어려운’, 이유의 접속사 because 뒤에 「주어 + 동사」가 온다.
writing.answer: Many people want to buy them because they are difficult to obtain.
writing.ko_prompt: 많은 사람들은 그것을 구하기 어렵기 때문에 사고 싶어 한다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
conditions: 접속사 As 로 문장을 시작할 것
비교급 less attractive 를 사용할 것
become 을 알맞은 형태로 쓸 것
writing.explanation_ko: 접속사 as 는 ‘~함에 따라, ~할수록’을 뜻하고, 주어 it 이 단수이므로 becomes 를 쓴다.
writing.answer: As more people buy the same product, it becomes less attractive to those consumers.
writing.ko_prompt: 더 많은 사람들이 같은 제품을 살수록, 그것은 그 소비자들에게 덜 매력적이 된다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: The snob effect is the ___________ of the bandwagon effect, which occurs when people buy a product simply because many others are buying it.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 스놉 효과는 밴드왜건 효과의 반대(the opposite)라고 했다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 「encourage + 목적어 + to부정사」 ‘~가 …하도록 부추기다’, 주격 관계대명사 that 이 products 를 수식하고 「help + 목적어 + 동사원형」이 이어진다.
writing.en_prompt: In contrast, the snob effect encourages people to choose products that help them stand out from the crowd.
writing.answer: 대조적으로, 스놉 효과는 사람들이 군중 속에서 돋보이게 해 주는 제품을 고르도록 부추긴다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 각각 한 단어로 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: People influenced by the snob effect value products that are rare or __(A)__, so companies release limited-edition products to create a sense of __(B)__ and exclusivity.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문 3번 문장의 rare or exclusive, 13번 문장의 a sense of rarity and exclusivity 에서 찾는다(뒤에 and exclusivity 가 이미 있으므로 (B)는 rarity).

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: rare 와 lose interest 를 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: Some consumers value products that are rare and lose interest when the products become popular.
writing.explanation_ko: 희귀한 제품을 중시하는 경향과 흔해지면 흥미를 잃는 결과를 한 문장에 담는다.
